sources.citation: Noukeu, Serge. 2002. Esquisse phonologique du Kada (Guidar). Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé I. iii+95 pp. (French)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Whole thesis is phonology: Chap. I Les tons pp. 8-10 (two tonemes, haut and bas: 'C'est le cas de la langue Kada qui utilise la hauteur mélodique à des fins distinctives', p. 8), Part II distribution of tonemes in mono-/di-/trisyllables pp. 52-53 (all H/B combinations occur), orthography chapter with tone graphemes. No mention of stress, accent, or intensity anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent scanned layer for accent/intensit/proémin/prosod: none). Open copy from MPI 'Language Description Heritage' REST endpoint (landing page bot-gated).
sources.venue: Mémoire de maîtrise, Université de Yaoundé I. iii+95 pp. (French)

sources.citation: Schuh, Russell G. 1984. Données de la langue kaɗa (gidar). Ms., Ahmadu Bello University Zaria / UCLA. 90 pp. (French)
sources.note: §2 Phonologie (pp. 6-19), §2.2.3 Tons p. 11: 'Le gidar n'a que deux tons au niveau phonématique, haut (H) et bas (B)', plus a falling tone analysed as H+B; nothing on stress or accent. Chapter 8 'Questions et Accentuation' (pp. 65 ff.) uses 'accentuation' for focus/emphasis of subject and object, not phonological stress; 8.1 notes no marked intonation difference between declaratives and yes/no questions. Internet Archive copy of the UCLA PDF (host now 404).

sources.note: Read online: the Kada inventory (source Noukeu 2002) lists exactly two tone segments, ˦ (high tone bar) and ˨ (low tone bar), beside the consonants and vowels, i.e. it encodes Gidar as a two-level-tone language (H, L), secondhand from Noukeu's 2002 Yaounde I phonology sketch (a work listed here, which states two tonemes haut/bas).
